reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates that acid-etching and N-doping produce a Pt-rich shell with M–N bonds in an HEA electrocatalyst, improving durability for the ORR. However, it provides no support for the premises that this treatment improves resistance to H2O/NO poisoning or enhances low-temperature CO/hydrocarbon oxidation in automotive exhaust, which are key to the hypothesis.
premises: Acid-etching a HEA creates a Pt-rich shell
Pt-rich shell and M–N bonds enhance durability
These modifications improve resistance to poisoning
Benefits transfer from electrocatalysis to automotive exhaust catalysis
